title: Better Compression of String
summary: Given a string compressed in the format of a character followed by its frequency, produce a new compressed string where each character appears only once, in alphabetical order, maintaining the frequency count.
statement: Given a string compressed in the format of a character followed by its frequency, produce a new compressed string where each character appears only once, in alphabetical order, maintaining the frequency count.
constraints: compressed is a nonempty concatenation of lowercase letters followed by positive decimal counts.
A letter may occur in multiple groups and counts may contain multiple digits.
Combine equal letters and output each present letter once in alphabetical order followed by its total count.
hints: Parsing must consume the entire consecutive digit run after each letter, then aggregate repeated letters.
Use an index scan and a frequency map, followed by sorted keys.
Read letter; advance through digits; add parsed integer; join sorted letter+total.
Every encoded group is consumed once and contributes exactly its count; sorting establishes the required canonical order.
editorial: Every encoded group is consumed once and contributes exactly its count; sorting establishes the required canonical order.

tests.explanation: The two c groups total ten; sorted output is a3b2c10.
The z counts total twenty and a sorts first, producing a1z20.
